items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with moments of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

The flags at City of Waterloo facilities had been at half-mast since the tragic events in Tumbler Ridge on February 11. This is the first Council meeting held since that date, and on behalf of Council, staff, and the City of Waterloo, I want to extend again our sincere condolences to all those who lost a family member or loved one, and to recognize all the lives which have been forever changed by this tragedy.
We continue to hold the people of Tumbler Ridge in our thoughts, sending strength to your community as you support one another through the coming weeks.

items.title: Open Air Fire By-law
notes: Deborah-Lynn Worden, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of a structured pilot program for backyard fires, addressing concerns outlined in a 2021 staff report, including safety, staffing and financial concerns. Deborah-Lynn Worden also spoke about the support from residents for such a program, as well as the benefits to the community.

items.title: Development Charge By-law Update –
notes: Stefan Krzeczunowicz, Hemson Consulting Ltd. gave a presentation outlining the Development Charges process including the passage of the proposed by-law, as well as the current and calculated rates of Development Charges for the City. Stefan Krzeczunowicz then responded to questions of Council. Brad Witzel and Michael Pugliese also responded to questions of Council.

Craig Sloss, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation detailing experience with Development Charges and affordability in the Region, as well as the year-over-year changes in the rates compared to the housing prices for the past three years. Craig Sloss also spoke in favour of the City not delaying the West Side Recreation Facility, as west Waterloo has the highest concentration of families with children and newcomers to Canada, and delaying it would disproportionately impact these communities.

Brian Santos, Advocacy Committee Member, Cornerstone Association of Realtors spoke against raising Development Charges in the City, as it impacts affordability and attainability for residents and newcomers to Waterloo. Brian Santos responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the process, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the meeting is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Freeman had a question for Kevin Van Ooteghem, wondering if the noise by- law can be implemented in an apartment building. Kevin Van Ooteghem responded that he would follow up with her.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Wright mentioned that Mount Zion Lutheran Church held their Black History Month service and community lunch this past Sunday, February 22. It was a highlight to join the congregation and celebrate the many accomplishments and contributions of Black Canadians and Black people around the world. It is also a celebration of the recipients of the Canadian Caribbean Association of Waterloo Region scholarship fund.
She and the other elected officials, including Councillor Roe, had the opportunity to serve the food to the community.

Councillor Roe attended the Black Pharmacy Professionals Conference this past weekend, February 20-22, at the University of Waterloo School of Pharmacy in Kitchener. Approximately 150 pharmacists and pharmacy students from across Canada attended the event. There was an awards ceremony, and great conversations about representation for health care providers that reflect people's lived experiences.
Mayor McCabe highlighted that Council for a Day is coming up on April 16. It’s open to grade five students in the City of Waterloo. They can share their one big idea to make the City even better.

motions.item_title: Mayor Dorothy McCabe – Provincial Plan for Consolidation of
motions.text: WHEREAS the Conservation Authorities Act, 1990 (the “Act”), originally enacted in 1946, was established to allow municipalities to form conservation authorities equipped to deliver local, watershed-based conservation, restoration, and natural resource management programs on behalf of both the province and municipalities; and, WHEREAS Ontario’s thirty-six (36) conservation authorities are each distinct, reflecting the unique environmental, geographic, and community needs of their respective watersheds; and, WHEREAS municipalities have long relied on their conservation authorities to tailor programs to local watershed priorities while ensuring fair and transparent costs for ratepayers; and, WHEREAS municipalities are best positioned to understand the needs of their local communities and environments, and the existing watershed- based structure enables effective, collaborative approaches to water conservation and resource management that cannot be replicated through centralized oversight; and, WHEREAS the Province of Ontario has not provided any information to municipalities regarding the financial and operational impact of the consolidation of Conservation Authorities to municipalities nor the conservation authorities; and, WHEREAS Bill 68 (Schedule 3) and ERO Posting 025-1257 propose consolidating Ontario’s 36 conservation authorities into seven regional authorities and creating the Ontario Provincial Conservation Agency, a Crown agency that would assume oversight and possess the authority to levy conservation authorities for its costs meaning municipalities may ultimately contribute all or a significant share of OPCA’s budget without having any meaningful role in shaping its governance, priorities, or strategic direction. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: THAT the City of Waterloo Council requests that the Minister of Environment, Conservation and Parks and the Chief Conservation Executive meaningfully consult with municipalities including the City of Waterloo to allow municipalities the opportunity to review the full financial, reserves and operational impacts that could affect local control and management of the floodplain areas watersheds and natural resources which Conservation Authorities were established to manage; AND THAT the Minister of Environment, Conservation and Parks and the Chief Conservation Executive meet with the GRCA leadership to consult regarding the regional model proposed which more closely aligns with existing Source Protection Regions; AND THAT a copy of this motion be forwarded to The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario; The Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of Environment, Conservation and Parks; local and area MPPs; the Grand River Conservation Authority (GRCA); the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO); the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario (AMCTO); and to the Region of Waterloo and local area municipalities.
